Check how many people match a people/search filter and see one masked row. 5 Firecrawl credits per call, including an empty page. Last names are masked; no email or phone. The id is real and works with people/email-find.

Find one person matching company and person filters, one row per page. 5 Firecrawl credits when a person comes back; an empty page costs nothing. No email or phone: follow with people/email-find using the returned id or LinkedIn URL. Use people/preview to check a filter first.

Start here for job discovery and employer comparison by hiring activity. Resolve a city/state with suggest_locations first when you need a location; pass next_cursor back as cursor for the following page. Sponsored cards are mixed in and page composition varies between fetches.
Resolve an employer name to its Glassdoor employer id, e.g. to filter search_jobs by employer_id. Returns an empty list for an unknown term.
Normalize a free-text role to the job titles Glassdoor knows before search_jobs. Returns an empty list when the site has no suggestion.
Resolve a place name to a Glassdoor location id before search_jobs. Returns an empty list for an unknown term.

Use to read hiring signal - which companies are posting which roles, where, and since when - or to find open roles. This is PDL's stored corpus of postings crawled from company career pages, not a live lookup: it holds deactivated postings alongside open ones, and by default returns both. For open roles send is_active true, add last_verified_min for how recently PDL must have seen the posting, and read deactivated_date and last_verified on each record before treating a role as open - nothing is checked against the employer at request time. One credit per record returned. Beta and entitlement-gated upstream: an account without access is answered as unavailable and not billed. Send field filters or query, never both. Learn the exact strings to filter on from autocomplete/suggest first, since several filters match canonical values only. Keep size at or below 50 to stay under the 1MB response cap, and paginate with scroll_token until it comes back absent or a 404 appears - which here means the scroll finished, not that the call failed.
